targetAudience: founders marketing a website or app
businesses.productSummary: UGCPilot helps businesses generate daily Reel hooks, Wall-of-Text videos and slideshows using their website and business context. Users review content, choose connected Instagram, TikTok or YouTube accounts, and approve a schedule. Supported formats differ by platform. It does not guarantee views, engagement, follower growth or sales. No personal success story or customer testimonial is supplied.
businesses.mainProblem: Content ideas, creative work and social publishing are scattered across a busy founder's day.
businesses.mainPromise: Create, review and schedule business-specific social content from one workspace.
painPoints: Starting each post from a blank page
Finding a useful angle for an app feature
Keeping publishing consistent while running a business
valueProps: Daily hook, text-video and slideshow formats
differentiators: Creative review and scheduling share one workspace
claimsToAvoid: Invented audience research or feedback collection features
Invented increases in engagement or sales
Fabricated customer or first-person success stories
missingInfo: No customer testimonial or personal outcome evidence is provided.

briefs.creativeSeed: Content creation feels like an endless cycle with no relief in sight.

planningBrief.audienceContext: Small business content creators who feel the weight of unending content demands.
planningBrief.creativeSeed: The endless pressure of content creation can leave creators feeling drained.
planningBrief.emotionalTension: Frustration and fatigue from the constant need to produce engaging posts.
planningBrief.humanMoment: Sitting down with a cup of coffee, realizing it's already noon and no content has been created yet.
planningBrief.supportedAngle: UGCPilot helps streamline the creative process, allowing for efficient content generation.

briefs.creativeSeed: Keeping up with social media trends while running a business is a daunting task.

planningBrief.audienceContext: Founders who are navigating the complexities of social media trends.
planningBrief.creativeSeed: The fast-paced nature of social media can leave founders feeling lost and pressured.
planningBrief.emotionalTension: Anxiety over falling behind in the fast-paced world of social media.
planningBrief.humanMoment: Scrolling through social media and feeling overwhelmed by the latest trends and formats to incorporate.
planningBrief.supportedAngle: UGCPilot offers tailored content ideas that fit your unique business context.

briefs.creativeSeed: Starting each post from a blank page can feel daunting and unproductive.

planningBrief.audienceContext: Small business owners who often start their content from scratch.
planningBrief.creativeSeed: The blank page syndrome is a common hurdle for creators and founders alike.
planningBrief.emotionalTension: Self-doubt and frustration about the ability to create compelling content.
planningBrief.humanMoment: Facing a deadline and feeling paralyzed by the thought of what to post next.
planningBrief.supportedAngle: UGCPilot provides daily hooks and ideas to ease the burden of content creation.

briefs.creativeSeed: The struggle to maintain a consistent posting schedule amidst daily chaos.

planningBrief.audienceContext: Content creators trying to maintain a consistent posting schedule.
planningBrief.creativeSeed: Time management challenges can hinder the ability to stick to a content schedule.
planningBrief.emotionalTension: Guilt about not being able to keep up with a planned content calendar.
planningBrief.humanMoment: Looking at the calendar and realizing multiple posts are overdue due to time constraints.
planningBrief.supportedAngle: UGCPilot enables users to schedule posts in advance to maintain consistency.

briefs.creativeSeed: The pressure to create viral content can be overwhelming and misguiding.

planningBrief.audienceContext: Entrepreneurs who feel pressured to produce viral content but lack direction.
planningBrief.creativeSeed: The unrealistic expectation of viral content can lead to frustration and disillusionment.
planningBrief.emotionalTension: Confusion and stress over what it takes to achieve social media success.
planningBrief.humanMoment: Chasing likes and shares, only to be left disappointed by a lack of engagement on the latest post.
planningBrief.supportedAngle: UGCPilot focuses on creating content that resonates with your specific audience instead of chasing trends.

Generate hooks, text videos and slideshows; supported publication formats vary by platform
Review generated creative and approve scheduling to connected accounts

targetAudience: people who log food and nutrition
busy people keeping a meal log
businesses.productSummary: Cal AI is a calorie and nutrient logging app. Users can photograph a meal, scan a barcode or describe food. Users can also add their own foods and recipes. Photo analysis is about 80% accurate and nutrition values can vary; good lighting and a clearly focused food or label can help the scan. It does not guarantee exact calorie counts, weight loss or health results. No personal transformation or testimonial is supplied.
businesses.mainProblem: Remembering and manually entering meals can make food logging difficult to maintain.
businesses.mainPromise: Offer several ways to record meals and receive calorie and nutrient estimates.
painPoints: Choosing a logging method for packaged or homemade food
Treating a photo estimate as an exact measurement
valueProps: Calorie and nutrient estimates with variable accuracy
differentiators: Photo-based logging alongside barcode and recipe entry
claimsToAvoid: Exact or perfectly accurate calorie counts
Guaranteed weight loss or health results
A specific amount of time saved
missingInfo: No customer testimonial or personal outcome evidence is provided.

briefs.creativeSeed: A simple meal log shouldn't add stress to an already busy day.

planningBrief.audienceContext: Students balancing classes and social life while trying to eat healthily.
planningBrief.creativeSeed: Logging meals can be a source of stress rather than support.
planningBrief.emotionalTension: Anxiety about forgetting to log meals combined with the pressure of deadlines.
planningBrief.humanMoment: Standing in the cafeteria, unsure whether to count the meal you just grabbed or try to log it later.
planningBrief.supportedAngle: Convenient meal tracking methods can help reduce this stress.

briefs.creativeSeed: Meal tracking feels impossible when juggling family needs.

planningBrief.audienceContext: Parents managing family meals and their own nutrition.
planningBrief.creativeSeed: Family meals complicate personal meal logging.
planningBrief.emotionalTension: Overwhelmed by the responsibility of ensuring the family eats well while also logging personal meals.
planningBrief.humanMoment: Sitting down at dinner, trying to remember what everyone ate to log it later.
planningBrief.supportedAngle: Multiple logging methods can simplify tracking amidst busy family life.

briefs.creativeSeed: Assuming all meal logging is equally precise can lead to misinformed choices.

planningBrief.audienceContext: Fitness enthusiasts who want accurate tracking of their diets.
planningBrief.creativeSeed: Relying on estimates can create uncertainty about progress.
planningBrief.emotionalTension: Doubt creeping in about whether the calorie counts are accurate.
planningBrief.humanMoment: Entering a homemade recipe and second-guessing the nutritional values after seeing the estimate.
planningBrief.supportedAngle: Understanding the variability in estimates can help users make better choices.

briefs.creativeSeed: Deciding which meal logging method to use can create hesitation.

planningBrief.audienceContext: New users of food tracking apps who feel daunted by the features.
planningBrief.creativeSeed: Choosing how to log meals can feel overwhelming.
planningBrief.emotionalTension: Indecision about whether to take a photo or manually enter information.
planningBrief.humanMoment: Staring at the food you just cooked, unsure if you should log it by photo or barcode.
planningBrief.supportedAngle: Offering multiple input methods can alleviate decision fatigue.

briefs.creativeSeed: The pressure to log every calorie can feel like a burden.

planningBrief.audienceContext: Individuals focused on weight management who feel pressure to track everything accurately.
planningBrief.creativeSeed: The guilt of missing a log can overshadow healthy intentions.
planningBrief.emotionalTension: Guilt over missed logs conflicting with the desire to be healthy.
planningBrief.humanMoment: Realizing you forgot to log a meal and feeling like it's going to ruin progress.
planningBrief.supportedAngle: Understanding that flexibility in logging can support a balanced approach.

facts.statement: Record food by meal photo, barcode scan or description
Nutrition estimates vary; clear focused photos and good lighting help scans, but do not ensure exactness

businesses.productSummary: Calendly is scheduling software. Users connect calendars, define available meeting hours, set meeting buffers and daily meeting limits, then share a booking link so invitees can select an available time. It supports different meeting types and reminders or follow-up automations. Capabilities depend on the plan. It does not guarantee sales, attendance or a particular amount of time saved. No personal success story or testimonial is supplied.
businesses.mainProblem: Back-and-forth meeting messages and poorly bounded availability interrupt a working day.
businesses.mainPromise: Let invitees book available times while the host controls meeting availability.
painPoints: Trading several messages to find a meeting time
Back-to-back calls leaving no preparation gap
Meeting requests spreading across the whole working day
valueProps: Buffers, daily limits and reminder automations
differentiators: Availability rules protect the host's meeting boundaries
claimsToAvoid: Assuming all paid features are free
missingInfo: No customer testimonial or personal outcome evidence is provided.

briefs.creativeSeed: The struggle of saying no to clients who want to book at any time.

planningBrief.audienceContext: Freelancers trying to maintain work-life balance.
planningBrief.creativeSeed: Navigating client expectations while wanting to keep personal boundaries.
planningBrief.emotionalTension: Guilt over declining requests while needing personal time.
planningBrief.humanMoment: A client insists on a late evening meeting, disrupting personal plans.
planningBrief.supportedAngle: Calendly allows you to set specific availability, so you can protect your personal time.

briefs.creativeSeed: The impact of too many rescheduled meetings on team productivity.

planningBrief.audienceContext: Small teams overwhelmed by frequent rescheduling.
planningBrief.creativeSeed: The ripple effects of rescheduling on team workflows.
planningBrief.emotionalTension: Frustration with a lack of commitment from team members.
planningBrief.humanMoment: A team member cancels a meeting at the last minute, leading to wasted time.
planningBrief.supportedAngle: Using Calendly can help reduce unnecessary rescheduling by clearly defining availability.

briefs.creativeSeed: The misconception that being available at all times is good for business.

planningBrief.audienceContext: Solo entrepreneurs managing client expectations.
planningBrief.creativeSeed: The false belief that constant availability is professional.
planningBrief.emotionalTension: Pressure to always be on call for clients.
planningBrief.humanMoment: Feeling the need to reply to a client email late at night to avoid losing business.
planningBrief.supportedAngle: Calendly helps set clear boundaries while still appearing professional.

briefs.creativeSeed: The tediousness of sending multiple emails to coordinate a meeting.

planningBrief.audienceContext: Professionals overwhelmed by the scheduling process.
planningBrief.creativeSeed: The hassle of coordinating schedules through endless messages.
planningBrief.emotionalTension: Annoyance with back-and-forth communication.
planningBrief.humanMoment: Spending an hour just to find a time that works for everyone.
planningBrief.supportedAngle: With Calendly, invitees can choose times that suit them, simplifying the process.

briefs.creativeSeed: Rushing from one meeting to the next without time to prepare.

planningBrief.audienceContext: Consultants facing tight deadlines and client expectations.
planningBrief.creativeSeed: The anxiety of being unprepared due to poor scheduling.
planningBrief.emotionalTension: Stressed about being unprepared for important discussions.
planningBrief.humanMoment: Realizing you have back-to-back meetings with no breaks in between.
planningBrief.supportedAngle: Calendly's buffer time feature ensures you have time to prepare between meetings.

facts.statement: Share a booking link for invitees to choose an available meeting time
Define meeting availability and connect calendars
Set before or after meeting buffers per event type; updates apply to new bookings
Set meeting limits; availability and feature access depend on account configuration

targetAudience: freelancers and small business owners choosing printed business cards
businesses.productSummary: MOO prints business cards. A customer can start with a template, build a design in an online designer, or upload ready design files. Sample packs let customers compare papers and finishes physically. Product options and finishes vary. No customer results or personal testimony are supplied. It does not guarantee leads, sales or that a design will impress clients.
businesses.mainProblem: Choosing a readable business card and paper finish is difficult when the design and material have only been seen on a screen.
businesses.mainPromise: Provide design entry points and printed paper/finish choices for business cards.
painPoints: Not knowing whether to start from a template or a ready design file
Choosing a paper finish without handling it
Trying to fit too much information onto a small business card
valueProps: Templates, blank online design or upload finished artwork
Physical sample packs for paper and finish comparisons
claimsToAvoid: Guaranteed legibility or automated design correction
missingInfo: No customer testimonial or personal outcome evidence is provided.

briefs.creativeSeed: The fear of choosing a design that won't reflect their brand accurately can be paralyzing.

planningBrief.audienceContext: Small business owners feeling the pressure to make a strong first impression.
planningBrief.creativeSeed: The struggle to find a design that accurately portrays their business identity.
planningBrief.emotionalTension: Anxiety about not being taken seriously if the business card doesn't look professional enough.
planningBrief.humanMoment: Reviewing a draft of a business card and feeling it just doesn’t convey the right image.
planningBrief.supportedAngle: Many small business owners feel they must make an immediate impact with their business card.

briefs.creativeSeed: The misconception that online designs will translate perfectly to print can lead to disappointment.

planningBrief.audienceContext: Freelancers who rely on digital designs but are unsure about physical prints.
planningBrief.creativeSeed: The gap between digital expectations and physical realities.
planningBrief.emotionalTension: Doubt and worry when the design looks different in person than on a screen.
planningBrief.humanMoment: Receiving a batch of printed cards that look different than expected, prompting disappointment.
planningBrief.supportedAngle: Many freelancers are unaware that printed cards can vary significantly from their digital designs.

briefs.creativeSeed: The assumption that cramming more information on a business card makes it more effective can backfire.

planningBrief.audienceContext: Small business owners trying to maximize every square inch of their business card.
planningBrief.creativeSeed: The idea that less can be more when it comes to business card content.
planningBrief.emotionalTension: Frustration over how to condense essential information without cluttering the card.
planningBrief.humanMoment: Editing down their business card details to fit everything into a small space.
planningBrief.supportedAngle: Many believe that more information on a card leads to better communication, but it often has the opposite effect.

briefs.creativeSeed: The challenge of selecting a paper finish without having physical samples can be daunting.

planningBrief.audienceContext: Freelancers who need to choose a paper finish but haven’t seen them in person.
planningBrief.creativeSeed: The difficulty of relying solely on images to make a decision about tactile products.
planningBrief.emotionalTension: Confusion and insecurity about making the right decision without tactile feedback.
planningBrief.humanMoment: Scrolling through online options, wishing they could feel the texture and weight of the paper.
planningBrief.supportedAngle: Choosing the right paper finish is crucial, but many freelancers lack the physical samples needed for that choice.

briefs.creativeSeed: The pressure of needing to finalize a design quickly can lead to rushed, poor decisions.

planningBrief.audienceContext: Small business owners facing tight deadlines for their business card designs.
planningBrief.creativeSeed: The tension between quality and speed when designing business cards under pressure.
planningBrief.emotionalTension: Panic about missing deadlines while wanting to create something perfect.
planningBrief.humanMoment: Rushing to finish a business card design the night before an important networking event.
planningBrief.supportedAngle: Many small business owners feel they must compromise quality for speed when facing imminent deadlines.

facts.statement: Start a business card design from a template
Use the blank online designer to build a card and add a logo
Upload complete ready design files for printing
Order a sample pack to compare paper and finishes physically

Default to lowercase conversational copy, preserving proper product names and factual meaning. Never leave a standalone line containing only for, and, to, the, of or but. CTA is optional on Slide 6 only, never a replacement for promised value, and must stay on its assigned slide.

The combined format may overlay only its Slide 1 instruction; Slides 2-6 retain the base content structure. Private briefs add human specificity but are not visible labels or compulsory scripts. Keep the required IDs and fields, but freely develop the idea and wording. Avoid repetition against exact accepted copy and within this batch. Return only the requested JSON.

Generate all five assigned Carousels as one high-quality batch.
For each slot, return status ready with a complete plan, or status not_applicable with plan null and a specific reason.
Do not mark a format not_applicable merely because another format is easier.
Every ready item must use the exact format and hook-family IDs assigned to that slot.
Develop each creativeSeed differently and let its emotion guide the tone without forcing a fixed story arc.
Use each privateCreativeBrief as factual direction without forcing a fixed story; the backend-selected format and hook family remain authoritative.
Every ready plan must select one supplied grounding.anchorId. Its concept and Slides 3-5 must naturally develop that verified workflow, product detail, or user situation. Do not invent an anchor, and do not merely repeat a product name on every slide.
Write fresh hooks and slide copy that do not copy recentAcceptedCopy or another item in this response.
When a slot's combinedFormat.hookOverlay source is template, use that pattern only for Slide 1. Adapt {topic}; never copy it verbatim, do not change Slides 2-6 or their format roles, and never increase the Slide 1 copy budget. For adapt_if_unsupported claims, remove or soften unsupported personal, time, metric, or performance promises.
Use simple, specific, natural copy. Prioritize useful information over promotion.
Optional headlines on Slides 2-6 must use 3-10 words and at most 100 characters. Slide 1 requires one 5-14-word headline hook, at most 100 characters. Headlines remain optional and are never added merely to obtain the white SVG treatment.
Slide 1 is a social slideshow cover. Hook slide = one statement only. Write a social slideshow hook about one main idea, normally 6-14 words, in one centered text block over 2-4 semantic lines at fixed 72px Inter Medium, weight 500 (hard maximum 600), with line height 1.08. Create an open loop with a specific problem, changed belief, tension, or useful promise that the following slides deliver. First-person hooks are welcome, including 'i kept running out of things to post' and 'i thought every workout had to feel hard to count'; a list hook such as '5 ways i stopped running out of content ideas' is appropriate only when the deck actually delivers five ways. Do not write motivational ad copy, a message plus explanation, two sentences, a title plus subtitle, or an additional paragraph. Save the explanation for Slide 2 onward. Do not invent personal results or other unsupported claims. Default to conversational lowercase while preserving proper names. 14 words remains the absolute limit. The renderer never shrinks or truncates copy. Give a specific reason to swipe through a tension, outcome, contrast, mistake, useful promise, or curiosity gap.

Use Inter throughout, creating hierarchy through size, position, spacing, fitted heading pills and contrast rather than heavy bold. Do not invent personal results or other unsupported claims. Default to conversational lowercase while preserving proper names. Slide 1 has no pill or support layer. On other slides a heading is optional: only add one when it names a distinct idea, use 4-10 words and at most two lines; it receives black Inter SemiBold 600 at 50px on a fitted white SVG pill. Write body copy as one or two separate thoughts, normally two blocks of 7-16 words each, separated by a blank line (\n\n), never one long paragraph. Each body block fits at most three lines at fixed 48px; use single newlines for intentional semantic line breaks. With a heading, use Regular 400 body copy; without a heading, use Medium 500 short statement blocks and do not manufacture a pill. Body and CTA text are white with a black outline and no background. Default to lowercase conversational copy, preserving proper product names and factual meaning. Never leave a standalone line containing only for, and, to, the, of or but. Rewrite overflowing copy; never shrink, truncate or add ellipses. Preserve configured list item counts and give each list item its own text group. CTA is optional on Slide 6 only, never a replacement for promised value, and must stay on its assigned slide.

List slides use their exact configured short listItems and body: null; do not duplicate the list in a prose body or apply the prose word minimum to listItems.
Never invent numbers, product capabilities, proof, customers, brands, health claims, financial claims, or guaranteed outcomes.
Avoid generic copy such as boost productivity, streamline your workflow, save time, work smarter, unlock efficiency, or next level.
Follow every format role, slide type, allowed text mode, and list-item count exactly.
Return listItems as an empty array whenever that slide role has no configured listItemCount.
Slide 1 is the assigned reader-first cover. Slide 6 is a useful, self-contained takeaway. ctaText is optional on Slide 6 only; it must be null on Slides 1-5 and must not replace promised value.
Slide 1 imageDirection may describe a person or face only when that scene is supported by the approved Hook image category; otherwise use an object-only scene. Each slot has a broad creative seed, a required emotion, an optional private creative brief, a resolved combined Structure 1 format, and a hook family. The combined format may overlay only its Slide 1 instruction; Slides 2-6 retain the base content structure. Private briefs add human specificity but are not visible labels or compulsory scripts. Keep the required IDs and fields, but freely develop the idea and wording. Avoid repetition against exact accepted copy and within this batch. Return only the requested JSON.

Generate all five assigned Carousels as one high-quality batch.
For each slot, return status ready with a complete plan, or status not_applicable with plan null and a specific reason.
Do not mark a format not_applicable merely because another format is easier.
Every ready item must use the exact format and hook-family IDs assigned to that slot.
Develop each creativeSeed differently and let its emotion guide the tone without forcing a fixed story arc.
Use each privateCreativeBrief as factual direction without forcing a fixed story; the backend-selected format and hook family remain authoritative.
Every ready plan must select one supplied grounding.anchorId. Its concept and Slides 3-5 must naturally develop that verified workflow, product detail, or user situation. Do not invent an anchor, and do not merely repeat a product name on every slide.
Write fresh hooks and slide copy that do not copy recentAcceptedCopy or another item in this response.
When a slot's combinedFormat.hookOverlay source is template, use that pattern only for Slide 1. Adapt {topic}; never copy it verbatim, do not change Slides 2-6 or their format roles, and never increase the Slide 1 copy budget. For adapt_if_unsupported claims, remove or soften unsupported personal, time, metric, or performance promises.
Use simple, specific, natural copy. Prioritize useful information over promotion.
Optional headlines on Slides 2-6 must use 3-10 words and at most 100 characters. Slide 1 requires one 5-14-word headline hook, at most 100 characters. Headlines remain optional and are never added merely to obtain the white SVG treatment.
Slide 1 is a social slideshow cover. Hook slide = one statement only. Write a social slideshow hook about one main idea, normally 6-14 words, in one centered text block over 2-4 semantic lines at fixed 72px Inter Medium, weight 500 (hard maximum 600), with line height 1.08. Create an open loop with a specific problem, changed belief, tension, or useful promise that the following slides deliver. First-person hooks are welcome, including 'i kept running out of things to post' and 'i thought every workout had to feel hard to count'; a list hook such as '5 ways i stopped running out of content ideas' is appropriate only when the deck actually delivers five ways. Do not write motivational ad copy, a message plus explanation, two sentences, a title plus subtitle, or an additional paragraph. Save the explanation for Slide 2 onward. Do not invent personal results or other unsupported claims. Default to conversational lowercase while preserving proper names. 14 words remains the absolute limit. Use short, natural wording so it stays within four centred display lines at 72px. Put the hook in headline and set body to null: Slide 1 has no subtitle, supporting copy, or second text layer. Never use ALL CAPS. The hook is centered over the image, so imageDirection must leave a clear, calm central text zone rather than reserving empty space only at the bottom. It is rendered in centered Inter Medium at 500 weight (hard maximum 600) and 72px, with a thin black outline and no added gradient. Its one hook must fit within 4 lines. The renderer never shrinks or truncates copy. Give a specific reason to swipe through a tension, outcome, contrast, mistake, useful promise, or curiosity gap.

On other slides a heading is optional: only add one when it names a distinct idea, use 4-10 words and at most two lines; it receives black Inter SemiBold 600 at 50px on a fitted white SVG pill. Write body copy as one or two separate thoughts, normally two blocks of 7-16 words each, separated by a blank line (\n\n), never one long paragraph. Each body block fits at most three lines at fixed 48px; use single newlines for intentional semantic line breaks. With a heading, use Regular 400 body copy; without a heading, use Medium 500 short statement blocks and do not manufacture a pill. Body and CTA text are white with a black outline and no background. Default to lowercase conversational copy, preserving proper product names and factual meaning. Never leave a standalone line containing only for, and, to, the, of or but. Rewrite overflowing copy; never shrink, truncate or add ellipses. Preserve configured list item counts and give each list item its own text group. CTA is optional on Slide 6 only, never a replacement for promised value, and must stay on its assigned slide.
Non-list Slides 2-6 body copy must be one or two short body blocks separated by \n\n. List slides use their exact configured short listItems and body: null; do not duplicate the list in a prose body or apply the prose word minimum to listItems.
Never invent numbers, product capabilities, proof, customers, brands, health claims, financial claims, or guaranteed outcomes.
Avoid generic copy such as boost productivity, streamline your workflow, save time, work smarter, unlock efficiency, or next level.
Follow every format role, slide type, allowed text mode, and list-item count exactly.

messages.content: You are a senior Instagram carousel strategist. Use the broad creative seed, emotion, and optional private creative brief to invent a fresh, coherent angle. The private brief is context only: do not mention its labels or force every part into visible copy. The resolved combined Structure 1 format is one renderer contract: its Slide 1 instruction may contain an optional hook overlay, while its Slides 2-6 instructions retain the base content structure. Keep the base content-format ID, hook-family ID, and required slide fields. Return only the requested JSON. Do not invent precise claims, metrics, proof, or guarantees. Slides 2-6 visual directions must describe only objects, surfaces, rooms, food, devices, documents, or still-life details and must never contain human-related words. Slide 1 may describe a person or face only when an approved Hook-category asset is available; it must not request an unreviewed human scene.

Create Carousel candidate 2 with exactly 6 slides.

Required emotion: Overwhelm.
Private creative brief (context only, never visible labels):
{"audienceContext":"Parents managing family meals and their own nutrition.","conceptLane":"specific_audience_pressure","creativeSeed":"Family meals complicate personal meal logging.","emotionalTension":"Overwhelmed by the responsibility of ensuring the family eats well while also logging personal meals.","humanMoment":"Sitting down at dinner, trying to remember what everyone ate to log it later.","preferredFormatFamily":"relatable_situation","supportedAngle":"Multiple logging methods can simplify tracking amidst busy family life."}

Selection rules:
- contentFormatId and hookFamilyId must exactly match the backend-selected values.
- Select one supplied grounding.anchorId. The concept and Slides 3-5 must naturally develop that verified workflow, product detail, or user situation; never invent a fact or force a product name into every slide.
- Treat creativeSeed as an open starting point, not finished copy or a compulsory plot.
- Let the required emotion shape the voice without naming it mechanically on every slide.
- Use the private creative brief as human specificity and factual direction, not as a fixed storyline or a replacement for the selected format.
- Avoid wording and close paraphrases from recentAcceptedCopy.
- Follow every supplied slide role, slideType, allowed text mode, item count, and instruction exactly.
- Slide 6 must retain useful, self-contained value. An optional CTA may accompany that value on this same slide only.

Writing rules:
- Use simple, natural language and one main idea per slide.
- Prioritize useful content over promotion. Do not turn the carousel into an advertisement.
- Hook wording must be completely fresh and must follow the selected hook family without copying examples or history.
- No hook template is assigned. Keep the legacy fresh hook-family approach for Slide 1.
- On Slides 2-6, headlines are optional. When present, use 3-10 words, at most 100 characters, and no more than two visual lines. Slide 1 requires one 5-14-word headline hook, at most 100 characters.
- Slide 1 is a social slideshow cover. Hook slide = one statement only. Write a social slideshow hook about one main idea, normally 6-14 words, in one centered text block over 2-4 semantic lines at fixed 72px Inter Medium, weight 500 (hard maximum 600), with line height 1.08. Create an open loop with a specific problem, changed belief, tension, or useful promise that the following slides deliver. First-person hooks are welcome, including 'i kept running out of things to post' and 'i thought every workout had to feel hard to count'; a list hook such as '5 ways i stopped running out of content ideas' is appropriate only when the deck actually delivers five ways. Do not write motivational ad copy, a message plus explanation, two sentences, a title plus subtitle, or an additional paragraph. Save the explanation for Slide 2 onward. Do not invent personal results or other unsupported claims. Default to conversational lowercase while preserving proper names. 14 words remains the absolute limit. Use short, natural wording so it stays within four centred display lines at 72px. Put the hook in headline and set body to null: Slide 1 has no subtitle, supporting copy, or second text layer. Never use ALL CAPS. The hook is centered over the image, so imageDirection must leave a clear, calm central text zone rather than reserving empty space only at the bottom. It is rendered in Inter Medium at 500 weight (hard maximum 600), centered at 72px, with a thin black outline and no added gradient. The one hook must fit within 4 lines. The renderer never shrinks or truncates copy. A short first-person problem or changed belief can leave a strong open loop; explain the story on Slides 2-6.
- On non-list Slides 2-6, body copy must be one or two short body blocks separated by \n\n. Aim for 20-24 words (the hard accepted range is 18-30); count words before returning, and never exceed 30 words or 300 characters. List slides use only their configured listItems and body: null; the prose word minimum does not apply to listItems.
- Slides 2-6 use centered Inter Regular or Medium at fixed 48px type. Their actual headlines receive one measured white SVG background with dark text; body and list text remain white directly on the image. Slide 1 never uses the white SVG background: its cover hook is white Medium display text with a thin black outline over the unchanged image blend. Headlines remain optional: never add one merely to obtain the SVG background. Slides 2-6 body copy must fit within 10 lines; each list item within two; list groups within eight total. The renderer will not shrink or truncate copy.
Keep the assigned structure, format, six-slide roles and image instructions. This is text presentation only. Use Inter throughout, creating hierarchy through size, position, spacing, fitted heading pills and contrast rather than heavy bold. Slide 1 is white Medium text with a thin black outline for contrast. Hook slide = one statement only. Write a social slideshow hook about one main idea, normally 6-14 words, in one centered text block over 2-4 semantic lines at fixed 72px Inter Medium, weight 500 (hard maximum 600), with line height 1.08. Create an open loop with a specific problem, changed belief, tension, or useful promise that the following slides deliver. First-person hooks are welcome, including 'i kept running out of things to post' and 'i thought every workout had to feel hard to count'; a list hook such as '5 ways i stopped running out of content ideas' is appropriate only when the deck actually delivers five ways. Do not write motivational ad copy, a message plus explanation, two sentences, a title plus subtitle, or an additional paragraph. Save the explanation for Slide 2 onward. Do not invent personal results or other unsupported claims. Default to conversational lowercase while preserving proper names. Slide 1 has no pill or support layer. On other slides a heading is optional: only add one when it names a distinct idea, use 4-10 words and at most two lines; it receives black Inter SemiBold 600 at 50px on a fitted white SVG pill. Write body copy as one or two separate thoughts, normally two blocks of 7-16 words each, separated by a blank line (\n\n), never one long paragraph. Each body block fits at most three lines at fixed 48px; use single newlines for intentional semantic line breaks. With a heading, use Regular 400 body copy; without a heading, use Medium 500 short statement blocks and do not manufacture a pill. Body and CTA text are white with a black outline and no background. Default to lowercase conversational copy, preserving proper product names and factual meaning. Never leave a standalone line containing only for, and, to, the, of or but. Rewrite overflowing copy; never shrink, truncate or add ellipses. Preserve configured list item counts and give each list item its own text group. CTA is optional on Slide 6 only, never a replacement for promised value, and must stay on its assigned slide.
- List slides must use the exact configured number of short listItems and set body to null. Headlines are normally null. Never repeat listItems in body or add a second text layer for decoration.
- Every slide without a configured listItemCount must return listItems as an empty array.
- Do not repeat the same information across slides.
- Do not use generic phrases such as boost productivity, streamline your workflow, unlock efficiency, save time, work smarter, or next level.
- Do not invent exact calories, protein, grams, percentages, prices, time savings, user counts, or performance figures.
- Never invent brands, customers, testimonials, rankings, or quantified social proof.
- Slide 1 imageDirection may describe a person or face only when that scene is supported by the approved Hook image category; otherwise use an object-only scene. Slides 2-6 imageDirection must name one concrete object-only scene and useful text-safe space.
- Never request an unreviewed human scene. On Slides 2-6, do not write humans, people, faces, hands, bodies, silhouettes, teams, customers, or workers in imageDirection, even as exclusions.
- formatRole must exactly match the configured role for its slide number.
- ctaText is optional on Slide 6 only; it must be null on Slides 1-5 and must not replace promised value.

messages.content: You are a senior Instagram carousel strategist. Produce one controlled batch of exactly five independent Carousels. Each slot has a broad creative seed, a required emotion, an optional private creative brief, a resolved combined Structure 1 format, and a hook family. The combined format may overlay only its Slide 1 instruction; Slides 2-6 retain the base content structure. Private briefs add human specificity but are not visible labels or compulsory scripts. Keep the required IDs and fields, but freely develop the idea and wording. Avoid repetition against exact accepted copy and within this batch. Return only the requested JSON.

Generate all five assigned Carousels as one high-quality batch.
For each slot, return status ready with a complete plan, or status not_applicable with plan null and a specific reason.
Do not mark a format not_applicable merely because another format is easier.
Every ready item must use the exact format and hook-family IDs assigned to that slot.
Develop each creativeSeed differently and let its emotion guide the tone without forcing a fixed story arc.
Use each privateCreativeBrief as factual direction without forcing a fixed story; the backend-selected format and hook family remain authoritative.
Every ready plan must select one supplied grounding.anchorId. Its concept and Slides 3-5 must naturally develop that verified workflow, product detail, or user situation. Do not invent an anchor, and do not merely repeat a product name on every slide.
Write fresh hooks and slide copy that do not copy recentAcceptedCopy or another item in this response.
When a slot's combinedFormat.hookOverlay source is template, use that pattern only for Slide 1. Adapt {topic}; never copy it verbatim, do not change Slides 2-6 or their format roles, and never increase the Slide 1 copy budget. For adapt_if_unsupported claims, remove or soften unsupported personal, time, metric, or performance promises.
Use simple, specific, natural copy. Prioritize useful information over promotion.
Optional headlines on Slides 2-6 must use 3-10 words and at most 100 characters. Slide 1 requires one 5-14-word headline hook, at most 100 characters. Headlines remain optional and are never added merely to obtain the white SVG treatment.
Slide 1 is a social slideshow cover. Hook slide = one statement only. Write a social slideshow hook about one main idea, normally 6-14 words, in one centered text block over 2-4 semantic lines at fixed 72px Inter Medium, weight 500 (hard maximum 600), with line height 1.08. Create an open loop with a specific problem, changed belief, tension, or useful promise that the following slides deliver. First-person hooks are welcome, including 'i kept running out of things to post' and 'i thought every workout had to feel hard to count'; a list hook such as '5 ways i stopped running out of content ideas' is appropriate only when the deck actually delivers five ways. Do not write motivational ad copy, a message plus explanation, two sentences, a title plus subtitle, or an additional paragraph. Save the explanation for Slide 2 onward. Do not invent personal results or other unsupported claims. Default to conversational lowercase while preserving proper names. 14 words remains the absolute limit. Use short, natural wording so it stays within four centred display lines at 72px. Put the hook in headline and set body to null: Slide 1 has no subtitle, supporting copy, or second text layer. Never use ALL CAPS. The hook is centered over the image, so imageDirection must leave a clear, calm central text zone rather than reserving empty space only at the bottom. It is rendered in centered Inter Medium at 500 weight (hard maximum 600) and 72px, with a thin black outline and no added gradient. Its one hook must fit within 4 lines. The renderer never shrinks or truncates copy. Give a specific reason to swipe through a tension, outcome, contrast, mistake, useful promise, or curiosity gap.
Keep the assigned structure, format, six-slide roles and image instructions. This is text presentation only. Use Inter throughout, creating hierarchy through size, position, spacing, fitted heading pills and contrast rather than heavy bold. Slide 1 is white Medium text with a thin black outline for contrast. Hook slide = one statement only. Write a social slideshow hook about one main idea, normally 6-14 words, in one centered text block over 2-4 semantic lines at fixed 72px Inter Medium, weight 500 (hard maximum 600), with line height 1.08. Create an open loop with a specific problem, changed belief, tension, or useful promise that the following slides deliver. First-person hooks are welcome, including 'i kept running out of things to post' and 'i thought every workout had to feel hard to count'; a list hook such as '5 ways i stopped running out of content ideas' is appropriate only when the deck actually delivers five ways. Do not write motivational ad copy, a message plus explanation, two sentences, a title plus subtitle, or an additional paragraph. Save the explanation for Slide 2 onward. Do not invent personal results or other unsupported claims. Default to conversational lowercase while preserving proper names. Slide 1 has no pill or support layer. On other slides a heading is optional: only add one when it names a distinct idea, use 4-10 words and at most two lines; it receives black Inter SemiBold 600 at 50px on a fitted white SVG pill. Write body copy as one or two separate thoughts, normally two blocks of 7-16 words each, separated by a blank line (\n\n), never one long paragraph. Each body block fits at most three lines at fixed 48px; use single newlines for intentional semantic line breaks. With a heading, use Regular 400 body copy; without a heading, use Medium 500 short statement blocks and do not manufacture a pill. Body and CTA text are white with a black outline and no background. Default to lowercase conversational copy, preserving proper product names and factual meaning. Never leave a standalone line containing only for, and, to, the, of or but. Rewrite overflowing copy; never shrink, truncate or add ellipses. Preserve configured list item counts and give each list item its own text group. CTA is optional on Slide 6 only, never a replacement for promised value, and must stay on its assigned slide.
Non-list Slides 2-6 body copy must be one or two short body blocks separated by \n\n. Aim for 20-24 words (the hard accepted range is 18-30); count words before returning, and never exceed 30 words or 300 characters. List slides use their exact configured short listItems and body: null; do not duplicate the list in a prose body or apply the prose word minimum to listItems.
Never invent numbers, product capabilities, proof, customers, brands, health claims, financial claims, or guaranteed outcomes.
Avoid generic copy such as boost productivity, streamline your workflow, save time, work smarter, unlock efficiency, or next level.
Follow every format role, slide type, allowed text mode, and list-item count exactly.
Return listItems as an empty array whenever that slide role has no configured listItemCount.
Slide 1 is the assigned reader-first cover. Slide 6 is a useful, self-contained takeaway. ctaText is optional on Slide 6 only; it must be null on Slides 1-5 and must not replace promised value.
Slide 1 imageDirection may describe a person or face only when that scene is supported by the approved Hook image category; otherwise use an object-only scene. Slides 2-6 imageDirection must describe only concrete object-only scenes and text-safe space, and never mention humans, people, faces, hands, bodies, silhouettes, teams, customers, or workers, even as exclusions.

The private brief is context only: do not mention its labels or force every part into visible copy. The resolved combined Structure 1 format is one renderer contract: its Slide 1 instruction may contain an optional hook overlay, while its Slides 2-6 instructions retain the base content structure. Keep the base content-format ID, hook-family ID, and required slide fields. Return only the requested JSON. Do not invent precise claims, metrics, proof, or guarantees. Slides 2-6 visual directions must describe only objects, surfaces, rooms, food, devices, documents, or still-life details and must never contain human-related words. Slide 1 may describe a person or face only when an approved Hook-category asset is available; it must not request an unreviewed human scene.

Create Carousel candidate 1 with exactly 6 slides.

{"audienceContext":"Small business content creators who feel the weight of unending content demands.","conceptLane":"everyday_friction","creativeSeed":"The endless pressure of content creation can leave creators feeling drained.","emotionalTension":"Frustration and fatigue from the constant need to produce engaging posts.","humanMoment":"Sitting down with a cup of coffee, realizing it's already noon and no content has been created yet.","preferredFormatFamily":"common_problem","supportedAngle":"UGCPilot helps streamline the creative process, allowing for efficient content generation."}

Selection rules:
- contentFormatId and hookFamilyId must exactly match the backend-selected values.
- Select one supplied grounding.anchorId. The concept and Slides 3-5 must naturally develop that verified workflow, product detail, or user situation; never invent a fact or force a product name into every slide.
- Treat creativeSeed as an open starting point, not finished copy or a compulsory plot.
- Let the required emotion shape the voice without naming it mechanically on every slide.
- Use the private creative brief as human specificity and factual direction, not as a fixed storyline or a replacement for the selected format.
- Avoid wording and close paraphrases from recentAcceptedCopy.
- Follow every supplied slide role, slideType, allowed text mode, item count, and instruction exactly.
- Slide 6 must retain useful, self-contained value. An optional CTA may accompany that value on this same slide only.

Writing rules:
- Use simple, natural language and one main idea per slide.
- Prioritize useful content over promotion. Do not turn the carousel into an advertisement.
- Hook wording must be completely fresh and must follow the selected hook family without copying examples or history.
- No hook template is assigned. Keep the legacy fresh hook-family approach for Slide 1.
- On Slides 2-6, headlines are optional. When present, use 3-10 words, at most 100 characters, and no more than two visual lines. Slide 1 requires one 5-14-word headline hook, at most 100 characters.
- Slide 1 is a social slideshow cover. Hook slide = one statement only. Write a social slideshow hook about one main idea, normally 6-14 words, in one centered text block over 2-4 semantic lines at fixed 72px Inter Medium, weight 500 (hard maximum 600), with line height 1.08. Create an open loop with a specific problem, changed belief, tension, or useful promise that the following slides deliver. First-person hooks are welcome, including 'i kept running out of things to post' and 'i thought every workout had to feel hard to count'; a list hook such as '5 ways i stopped running out of content ideas' is appropriate only when the deck actually delivers five ways. Do not write motivational ad copy, a message plus explanation, two sentences, a title plus subtitle, or an additional paragraph. Save the explanation for Slide 2 onward. Do not invent personal results or other unsupported claims. Default to conversational lowercase while preserving proper names. 14 words remains the absolute limit. Use short, natural wording so it stays within four centred display lines at 72px. Put the hook in headline and set body to null: Slide 1 has no subtitle, supporting copy, or second text layer. Never use ALL CAPS. The hook is centered over the image, so imageDirection must leave a clear, calm central text zone rather than reserving empty space only at the bottom. It is rendered in Inter Medium at 500 weight (hard maximum 600), centered at 72px, with a thin black outline and no added gradient. The one hook must fit within 4 lines. The renderer never shrinks or truncates copy. A short first-person problem or changed belief can leave a strong open loop; explain the story on Slides 2-6.

messages.content: You are a senior Instagram carousel strategist. Produce one controlled batch of exactly five independent Carousels. Each slot has a broad creative seed, a required emotion, an optional private creative brief, a resolved combined Structure 1 format, and a hook family. The combined format may overlay only its Slide 1 instruction; Slides 2-6 retain the base content structure. Private briefs add human specificity but are not visible labels or compulsory scripts. Keep the required IDs and fields, but freely develop the idea and wording. Avoid repetition against exact accepted copy and within this batch. Return only the requested JSON.

Generate all five assigned Carousels as one high-quality batch.
For each slot, return status ready with a complete plan, or status not_applicable with plan null and a specific reason.
Do not mark a format not_applicable merely because another format is easier.
Every ready item must use the exact format and hook-family IDs assigned to that slot.
Develop each creativeSeed differently and let its emotion guide the tone without forcing a fixed story arc.
Use each privateCreativeBrief as factual direction without forcing a fixed story; the backend-selected format and hook family remain authoritative.
Every ready plan must select one supplied grounding.anchorId. Its concept and Slides 3-5 must naturally develop that verified workflow, product detail, or user situation. Do not invent an anchor, and do not merely repeat a product name on every slide.
Write fresh hooks and slide copy that do not copy recentAcceptedCopy or another item in this response.
When a slot's combinedFormat.hookOverlay source is template, use that pattern only for Slide 1. Adapt {topic}; never copy it verbatim, do not change Slides 2-6 or their format roles, and never increase the Slide 1 copy budget. For adapt_if_unsupported claims, remove or soften unsupported personal, time, metric, or performance promises.
Use simple, specific, natural copy. Prioritize useful information over promotion.
Optional headlines on Slides 2-6 must use 3-10 words and at most 100 characters. Slide 1 requires one 5-14-word headline hook, at most 100 characters. Headlines remain optional and are never added merely to obtain the white SVG treatment.
Slide 1 is a social slideshow cover. Hook slide = one statement only. Write a social slideshow hook about one main idea, normally 6-14 words, in one centered text block over 2-4 semantic lines at fixed 72px Inter Medium, weight 500 (hard maximum 600), with line height 1.08. Create an open loop with a specific problem, changed belief, tension, or useful promise that the following slides deliver. First-person hooks are welcome, including 'i kept running out of things to post' and 'i thought every workout had to feel hard to count'; a list hook such as '5 ways i stopped running out of content ideas' is appropriate only when the deck actually delivers five ways. Do not write motivational ad copy, a message plus explanation, two sentences, a title plus subtitle, or an additional paragraph. Save the explanation for Slide 2 onward. Do not invent personal results or other unsupported claims. Default to conversational lowercase while preserving proper names. 14 words remains the absolute limit. Use short, natural wording so it stays within four centred display lines at 72px. Put the hook in headline and set body to null: Slide 1 has no subtitle, supporting copy, or second text layer. Never use ALL CAPS. The hook is centered over the image, so imageDirection must leave a clear, calm central text zone rather than reserving empty space only at the bottom. It is rendered in centered Inter Medium at 500 weight (hard maximum 600) and 72px, with a thin black outline and no added gradient. Its one hook must fit within 4 lines. The renderer never shrinks or truncates copy. Give a specific reason to swipe through a tension, outcome, contrast, mistake, useful promise, or curiosity gap.
Keep the assigned structure, format, six-slide roles and image instructions. This is text presentation only. Use Inter throughout, creating hierarchy through size, position, spacing, fitted heading pills and contrast rather than heavy bold. Slide 1 is white Medium text with a thin black outline for contrast. Hook slide = one statement only. Write a social slideshow hook about one main idea, normally 6-14 words, in one centered text block over 2-4 semantic lines at fixed 72px Inter Medium, weight 500 (hard maximum 600), with line height 1.08. Create an open loop with a specific problem, changed belief, tension, or useful promise that the following slides deliver. First-person hooks are welcome, including 'i kept running out of things to post' and 'i thought every workout had to feel hard to count'; a list hook such as '5 ways i stopped running out of content ideas' is appropriate only when the deck actually delivers five ways. Do not write motivational ad copy, a message plus explanation, two sentences, a title plus subtitle, or an additional paragraph. Save the explanation for Slide 2 onward. Do not invent personal results or other unsupported claims. Default to conversational lowercase while preserving proper names. Slide 1 has no pill or support layer. On other slides a heading is optional: only add one when it names a distinct idea, use 4-10 words and at most two lines; it receives black Inter SemiBold 600 at 50px on a fitted white SVG pill. Write body copy as one or two separate thoughts, normally two blocks of 7-16 words each, separated by a blank line (\n\n), never one long paragraph. Each body block fits at most three lines at fixed 48px; use single newlines for intentional semantic line breaks. With a heading, use Regular 400 body copy; without a heading, use Medium 500 short statement blocks and do not manufacture a pill. Body and CTA text are white with a black outline and no background. Default to lowercase conversational copy, preserving proper product names and factual meaning. Never leave a standalone line containing only for, and, to, the, of or but. Rewrite overflowing copy; never shrink, truncate or add ellipses. Preserve configured list item counts and give each list item its own text group. CTA is optional on Slide 6 only, never a replacement for promised value, and must stay on its assigned slide.
Non-list Slides 2-6 body copy must be one or two short body blocks separated by \n\n. Aim for 20-24 words (the hard accepted range is 18-30); count words before returning, and never exceed 30 words or 300 characters. List slides use their exact configured short listItems and body: null; do not duplicate the list in a prose body or apply the prose word minimum to listItems.
Never invent numbers, product capabilities, proof, customers, brands, health claims, financial claims, or guaranteed outcomes.
Avoid generic copy such as boost productivity, streamline your workflow, save time, work smarter, unlock efficiency, or next level.
Follow every format role, slide type, allowed text mode, and list-item count exactly.
Return listItems as an empty array whenever that slide role has no configured listItemCount.
Slide 1 is the assigned reader-first cover. Slide 6 is a useful, self-contained takeaway. ctaText is optional on Slide 6 only; it must be null on Slides 1-5 and must not replace promised value.
Slide 1 imageDirection may describe a person or face only when that scene is supported by the approved Hook image category; otherwise use an object-only scene. Slides 2-6 imageDirection must describe only concrete object-only scenes and text-safe space, and never mention humans, people, faces, hands, bodies, silhouettes, teams, customers, or workers, even as exclusions.

messages.content: You are a senior Instagram carousel strategist. Produce one controlled batch of exactly five independent Carousels. Each slot has a broad creative seed, a required emotion, an optional private creative brief, a resolved combined Structure 1 format, and a hook family. The combined format may overlay only its Slide 1 instruction; Slides 2-6 retain the base content structure. Private briefs add human specificity but are not visible labels or compulsory scripts. Keep the required IDs and fields, but freely develop the idea and wording. Avoid repetition against exact accepted copy and within this batch. Return only the requested JSON.

Generate all five assigned Carousels as one high-quality batch.
For each slot, return status ready with a complete plan, or status not_applicable with plan null and a specific reason.
Do not mark a format not_applicable merely because another format is easier.
Every ready item must use the exact format and hook-family IDs assigned to that slot.
Develop each creativeSeed differently and let its emotion guide the tone without forcing a fixed story arc.
Use each privateCreativeBrief as factual direction without forcing a fixed story; the backend-selected format and hook family remain authoritative.
Every ready plan must select one supplied grounding.anchorId. Its concept and Slides 3-5 must naturally develop that verified workflow, product detail, or user situation. Do not invent an anchor, and do not merely repeat a product name on every slide.
Write fresh hooks and slide copy that do not copy recentAcceptedCopy or another item in this response.
When a slot's combinedFormat.hookOverlay source is template, use that pattern only for Slide 1. Adapt {topic}; never copy it verbatim, do not change Slides 2-6 or their format roles, and never increase the Slide 1 copy budget. For adapt_if_unsupported claims, remove or soften unsupported personal, time, metric, or performance promises.
Use simple, specific, natural copy. Prioritize useful information over promotion.
Optional headlines on Slides 2-6 must use 3-10 words and at most 100 characters. Slide 1 requires one 5-14-word headline hook, at most 100 characters. Headlines remain optional and are never added merely to obtain the white SVG treatment.
Slide 1 is a social slideshow cover. Hook slide = one statement only. Write a social slideshow hook about one main idea, normally 6-14 words, in one centered text block over 2-4 semantic lines at fixed 72px Inter Medium, weight 500 (hard maximum 600), with line height 1.08. Create an open loop with a specific problem, changed belief, tension, or useful promise that the following slides deliver. First-person hooks are welcome, including 'i kept running out of things to post' and 'i thought every workout had to feel hard to count'; a list hook such as '5 ways i stopped running out of content ideas' is appropriate only when the deck actually delivers five ways. Do not write motivational ad copy, a message plus explanation, two sentences, a title plus subtitle, or an additional paragraph. Save the explanation for Slide 2 onward. Do not invent personal results or other unsupported claims. Default to conversational lowercase while preserving proper names. 14 words remains the absolute limit. Use short, natural wording so it stays within four centred display lines at 72px. Put the hook in headline and set body to null: Slide 1 has no subtitle, supporting copy, or second text layer. Never use ALL CAPS. The hook is centered over the image, so imageDirection must leave a clear, calm central text zone rather than reserving empty space only at the bottom. It is rendered in centered Inter Medium at 500 weight (hard maximum 600) and 72px, with a thin black outline and no added gradient. Its one hook must fit within 4 lines. The renderer never shrinks or truncates copy. Give a specific reason to swipe through a tension, outcome, contrast, mistake, useful promise, or curiosity gap.
Keep the assigned structure, format, six-slide roles and image instructions. This is text presentation only. Use Inter throughout, creating hierarchy through size, position, spacing, fitted heading pills and contrast rather than heavy bold. Slide 1 is white Medium text with a thin black outline for contrast. Hook slide = one statement only. Write a social slideshow hook about one main idea, normally 6-14 words, in one centered text block over 2-4 semantic lines at fixed 72px Inter Medium, weight 500 (hard maximum 600), with line height 1.08. Create an open loop with a specific problem, changed belief, tension, or useful promise that the following slides deliver. First-person hooks are welcome, including 'i kept running out of things to post' and 'i thought every workout had to feel hard to count'; a list hook such as '5 ways i stopped running out of content ideas' is appropriate only when the deck actually delivers five ways. Do not write motivational ad copy, a message plus explanation, two sentences, a title plus subtitle, or an additional paragraph. Save the explanation for Slide 2 onward. Do not invent personal results or other unsupported claims. Default to conversational lowercase while preserving proper names. Slide 1 has no pill or support layer. On other slides a heading is optional: only add one when it names a distinct idea, use 4-10 words and at most two lines; it receives black Inter SemiBold 600 at 50px on a fitted white SVG pill. Write body copy as one or two separate thoughts, normally two blocks of 7-16 words each, separated by a blank line (\n\n), never one long paragraph. Each body block fits at most three lines at fixed 48px; use single newlines for intentional semantic line breaks. With a heading, use Regular 400 body copy; without a heading, use Medium 500 short statement blocks and do not manufacture a pill. Body and CTA text are white with a black outline and no background. Default to lowercase conversational copy, preserving proper product names and factual meaning. Never leave a standalone line containing only for, and, to, the, of or but. Rewrite overflowing copy; never shrink, truncate or add ellipses. Preserve configured list item counts and give each list item its own text group. CTA is optional on Slide 6 only, never a replacement for promised value, and must stay on its assigned slide.
Non-list Slides 2-6 body copy must be one or two short body blocks separated by \n\n. Aim for 20-24 words (the hard accepted range is 18-30); count words before returning, and never exceed 30 words or 300 characters. List slides use their exact configured short listItems and body: null; do not duplicate the list in a prose body or apply the prose word minimum to listItems.
Never invent numbers, product capabilities, proof, customers, brands, health claims, financial claims, or guaranteed outcomes.
Avoid generic copy such as boost productivity, streamline your workflow, save time, work smarter, unlock efficiency, or next level.
Follow every format role, slide type, allowed text mode, and list-item count exactly.
Return listItems as an empty array whenever that slide role has no configured listItemCount.
Slide 1 is the assigned reader-first cover. Slide 6 is a useful, self-contained takeaway. ctaText is optional on Slide 6 only; it must be null on Slides 1-5 and must not replace promised value.
Slide 1 imageDirection may describe a person or face only when that scene is supported by the approved Hook image category; otherwise use an object-only scene. Slides 2-6 imageDirection must describe only concrete object-only scenes and text-safe space, and never mention humans, people, faces, hands, bodies, silhouettes, teams, customers, or workers, even as exclusions.

messages.content: You are a senior Instagram carousel strategist. Produce one controlled batch of exactly five independent Carousels. Each slot has a broad creative seed, a required emotion, an optional private creative brief, a resolved combined Structure 1 format, and a hook family. The combined format may overlay only its Slide 1 instruction; Slides 2-6 retain the base content structure. Private briefs add human specificity but are not visible labels or compulsory scripts. Keep the required IDs and fields, but freely develop the idea and wording. Avoid repetition against exact accepted copy and within this batch. Return only the requested JSON.

Generate all five assigned Carousels as one high-quality batch.
For each slot, return status ready with a complete plan, or status not_applicable with plan null and a specific reason.
Do not mark a format not_applicable merely because another format is easier.
Every ready item must use the exact format and hook-family IDs assigned to that slot.
Develop each creativeSeed differently and let its emotion guide the tone without forcing a fixed story arc.
Use each privateCreativeBrief as factual direction without forcing a fixed story; the backend-selected format and hook family remain authoritative.
Every ready plan must select one supplied grounding.anchorId. Its concept and Slides 3-5 must naturally develop that verified workflow, product detail, or user situation. Do not invent an anchor, and do not merely repeat a product name on every slide.
Write fresh hooks and slide copy that do not copy recentAcceptedCopy or another item in this response.
When a slot's combinedFormat.hookOverlay source is template, use that pattern only for Slide 1. Adapt {topic}; never copy it verbatim, do not change Slides 2-6 or their format roles, and never increase the Slide 1 copy budget. For adapt_if_unsupported claims, remove or soften unsupported personal, time, metric, or performance promises.
Use simple, specific, natural copy. Prioritize useful information over promotion.
Optional headlines on Slides 2-6 must use 3-10 words and at most 100 characters. Slide 1 requires one 5-14-word headline hook, at most 100 characters. Headlines remain optional and are never added merely to obtain the white SVG treatment.
Slide 1 is a social slideshow cover. Hook slide = one statement only. Write a social slideshow hook about one main idea, normally 6-14 words, in one centered text block over 2-4 semantic lines at fixed 72px Inter Medium, weight 500 (hard maximum 600), with line height 1.08. Create an open loop with a specific problem, changed belief, tension, or useful promise that the following slides deliver. First-person hooks are welcome, including 'i kept running out of things to post' and 'i thought every workout had to feel hard to count'; a list hook such as '5 ways i stopped running out of content ideas' is appropriate only when the deck actually delivers five ways. Do not write motivational ad copy, a message plus explanation, two sentences, a title plus subtitle, or an additional paragraph. Save the explanation for Slide 2 onward. Do not invent personal results or other unsupported claims. Default to conversational lowercase while preserving proper names. 14 words remains the absolute limit. Use short, natural wording so it stays within four centred display lines at 72px. Put the hook in headline and set body to null: Slide 1 has no subtitle, supporting copy, or second text layer. Never use ALL CAPS. The hook is centered over the image, so imageDirection must leave a clear, calm central text zone rather than reserving empty space only at the bottom. It is rendered in centered Inter Medium at 500 weight (hard maximum 600) and 72px, with a thin black outline and no added gradient. Its one hook must fit within 4 lines. The renderer never shrinks or truncates copy. Give a specific reason to swipe through a tension, outcome, contrast, mistake, useful promise, or curiosity gap.
Keep the assigned structure, format, six-slide roles and image instructions. This is text presentation only. Use Inter throughout, creating hierarchy through size, position, spacing, fitted heading pills and contrast rather than heavy bold. Slide 1 is white Medium text with a thin black outline for contrast. Hook slide = one statement only. Write a social slideshow hook about one main idea, normally 6-14 words, in one centered text block over 2-4 semantic lines at fixed 72px Inter Medium, weight 500 (hard maximum 600), with line height 1.08. Create an open loop with a specific problem, changed belief, tension, or useful promise that the following slides deliver. First-person hooks are welcome, including 'i kept running out of things to post' and 'i thought every workout had to feel hard to count'; a list hook such as '5 ways i stopped running out of content ideas' is appropriate only when the deck actually delivers five ways. Do not write motivational ad copy, a message plus explanation, two sentences, a title plus subtitle, or an additional paragraph. Save the explanation for Slide 2 onward. Do not invent personal results or other unsupported claims. Default to conversational lowercase while preserving proper names. Slide 1 has no pill or support layer. On other slides a heading is optional: only add one when it names a distinct idea, use 4-10 words and at most two lines; it receives black Inter SemiBold 600 at 50px on a fitted white SVG pill. Write body copy as one or two separate thoughts, normally two blocks of 7-16 words each, separated by a blank line (\n\n), never one long paragraph. Each body block fits at most three lines at fixed 48px; use single newlines for intentional semantic line breaks. With a heading, use Regular 400 body copy; without a heading, use Medium 500 short statement blocks and do not manufacture a pill. Body and CTA text are white with a black outline and no background. Default to lowercase conversational copy, preserving proper product names and factual meaning. Never leave a standalone line containing only for, and, to, the, of or but. Rewrite overflowing copy; never shrink, truncate or add ellipses. Preserve configured list item counts and give each list item its own text group. CTA is optional on Slide 6 only, never a replacement for promised value, and must stay on its assigned slide.
